text:
maria: Heads up — around 08:12 UTC we saw a spike of preemptible GPU termination notices across us-west2-spot pool, ~8 nodes in ~90s. Cluster-autoscaler started aggressive drains and we ended up with ~30 pending GPU pods for ~7m before fallback kicked in. Logs below.

devon: ugh, saw that. any indication it was a single provider batch or region-level maintenance? :thinking:

maria: cloud provider published short notice window (30-60s) for maintenance. but the termination webhook was flapping, some nodes sent notice then retracted, CA still began eviction path.

kai: CA settings currently: scale-down-delay=10m, scale-up-cooldown=0s, balancing-expander. But our drain logic triggers immediately on termination taint => pods get evicted before fallback on-demand nodes spin up.

lee: fallback pool (on-demand-gpu-fallback) didn't spin up because we hit regional quota; autoscaler queued requests but cloud returned 429/QuotaExceeded. That explains the 7m backlog.

maria: snippet from controller logs:
```
I0316 08:12:21.234] node-watch: node/spot-gpu-12: termination-notice received
I0316 08:12:21.600] pod-evict: evicting 4 pods from node/spot-gpu-12
I0316 08:12:22.010] termination-retracted: node/spot-gpu-12 — notice cleared
I0316 08:12:23.800] ca-scale: requested 4 nodes in on-demand-gpu-fallback -> 429 QuotaExceeded
```

devon: two immediate action items I see: (1) stop immediate evictions on transient termination notices, (2) add a short pause window to allow fallback pools/quotas to resolve before draining.

kai: agree. propose adding an explicit "preemptible-termination-grace" annotation on nodepools. If set, the node controller will wait X seconds before starting eviction pipeline unless notice persists. e.g.
```
kubectl annotate nodepool spot-gpu --overwrite preemptible-termination-grace=45
```

lee: also add autoscaler change: switch to less aggressive pod eviction on preemptible taint and increase scale-up parallelism for fallback pools. maybe bump max-node-provisioning-per-second for on-demand pools.

infra-oncall: tagging for follow-up: quota owner paged, we'll request quota bump for us-west2 and prewarm one small on-demand capacity in us-west2 to act as absorb buffer for critical jobs.

autoscaler-bot: [info] Proposed CA patch: add flag --preemptible-drain-wait=30s and honor node annotation preemptible-termination-grace. Draft PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ca/merge/1824

maria: cost note — adding a tiny reserved on-demand buffer (1-2 small GPUs) increases baseline spend ~+8-10% for gpu-heavy clusters, but reduces failed job retries and user impact. We should compare SLO hit cost vs reserved cost.

devon: for short-term mitigation I'll: (a) flip CA to respect --preemptible-drain-wait=45s in staging, (b) enable fallback pool autoscaler surge increase, (c) create alert for >3 termination notices in 2m for a region. Will report back in 30m.

kai: longer term: add logic to route non-critical batch pods to a lower-priority preemptible-only nodepool and pin critical latency jobs to on-demand or dedicated. Also consider multi-region fallback automation (spin fallback in us-east1 if us-west2 quota fails).

lee: FYI I added a small change to nodepool Terraform to include preemptible-termination-grace default=30 in next plan, and created issue for quota automation: #INFRA-547.

maria: thanks — once we validate the staging CA flag I'll push to prod with the reserved buffer enabled. Also add a quick runbook step: if termination notices spike, check quota and if quota blocked, manually scale a small on-demand pool while quota is resolved.

devon: noted. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: closing loop — quota raised for us-west2 by cloud team, fallback pool prewarmed, CA flag landed in staging. We'll monitor next 24h.

maria: moving to post-incident tasks: update runbook, add telemetry for notice-retract events, and run a chaos test that pulses termination notices for 60-90s to validate grace window.
